title.narrative: Global Polio Eradication Initiative Core Contributions for Financial Years 2022-23 to 2026-27

description.narrative: This investment provides core funding to the World Health Organization for the Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI). Australia's contribution will provide funding and technical assistance for polio surveillance, monitoring, supplementary immunisation campaigns and outbreak responses. It will help strengthen health and routine immunisation systems and ensure they are sustainably financed and managed. The total value of this investment is $36.05 million over five years, starting 2022-2023. It is the second phase of GPEI funding , following on from investment INL872 Polio and Routine Immunization 2015-2022.

title.narrative: Global Polio Eradication Initiative Core Contributions for Financial Years 2022-23 to 2026-27

description.narrative: Australia, through our contribution to the Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI), supported efforts to permanently interrupt all poliovirus transmission in endemic countries and stop circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus (cVDPV) transmission and prevent outbreaks in non-endemic countries. In 2023, despite significant geopolitical and environmental challenges in the two remaining wild poliovirus (WPV) endemic countries, Pakistan and Afghanistan, the polio programme continued to reach more children than in previous years. To help reduce cVPVC transmission, in 2023 GPEI supported delivery and administration of nearly 1 billion doses of nOPV2, a comparably safe, effective but more genetically stable version of the existing oral polio vaccine in 35 countries to help bring Vaccine-derived poliovirus outbreaks under control. And while 23 Countries reported cVDPV cases in 2023, compared to 21 in 2022, the number of cases went down significantly from 393 cVDPV2 cases in 2023 compared to 687 in 2022.

Australia, through support for the Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI), contributes to improving health system capacities in the areas of surveillance, routine immunisation, and outbreak response. This includes direct provision of primary health care services in partnership with others, as well as training and capacity building of health personnel on topics such as community mobilisation and public health communications. GPEI provides specialist technical assistance including in the areas of surveillance, laboratory systems, cold chains and supply chain management and provides cold-chain equipment where needed, along with vaccines (oral and injectable), and disposable injection supplies. In addition, GPEI supports countries to make policy and regulatory adjustments to enable the introduction and use of inactivated polio vaccine and novel oral polio vaccines and in partnership with WHO, Gavi and UNICEF, they have significantly improved procurement forecasting and distribution systems for polio vaccination, strengthening procurement forecasting and distribution systems for other vaccines.

GPEI makes a significant contribution to health system capacities in the fields of surveillance, routine immunisation and outbreak response in Afghanistan and Pakistan, and at sub-national level in several other countries. GPEI trains thousands of polio program workers, and is constantly recruiting, training and re-training them in response to the program's changing needs. GPEI-supported polio program workers have community-level outbreak response capacities, which can be leveraged for other disease outbreaks. GPEI also invests in specialist technical assistance for surveillance, laboratory systems, cold chain and supply chain management. GPEI has supported the use of waste-water surveillance, which has broad application for disease monitoring beyond polio. Following WHO Prequalification in December 2023, GPEI is continuing to support the use of the novel Oral Polio Vaccine (Type 2), and novel oral polio vaccines (Types 1 and 3) are also being developed. In partnership with WHO, Gavi and UNICEF, GPEI has significantly improved procurement forecasting and distribution systems for polio vaccination, which are also used for other vaccines - this is a significant contribution to strengthening routine immunisation systems.

Global Polio Eradication Initiative's (GPEI’s) investments in surveillance systems, polio workers, and outbreak response capacities have significantly strengthened countries’ abilities to detect and respond to infectious disease outbreaks. Afghanistan and Pakistan have particularly benefited from GPEI's support. GPEI has built and sustained a Global Polio Laboratory Network made up 146 laboratories in 92 countries across all six WHO regions (including the South-East Asia and Western Pacific regions), which is central to surveillance systems for polio and other infectious diseases. ‍ In countries affected by polio outbreaks, GPEI has invested significantly in developing and sustaining Emergency Operations Centres to manage outbreak responses. These capacities can also be leveraged for other infectious diseases. ‍ In 2024, GPEI intensified polio surveillance in Gaza, with GPEI partners WHO and UNICEF supporting vaccination campaigns in the area in late 2024.
